text:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — i dug through the scheduler pr and a couple things stood out. we haven't clearly defined the grpc/http boundary between the runtime and the admission/scheduler layer. should runtime expose a small admission API or should scheduler push batches in?

ryan: +1 on explicit boundary. pushing batches from scheduler into runtime feels cleaner for backpressure handling. runtime implements an AddBatch(Batch) rpc and returns a short ack.

kevin: do we lose visibility if scheduler pushes? how do we measure token-level latency and queueing time then? we need hooks for per-request telemetry.

maria: exactly — telemetry hooks are the main concern. idea: keep AddBatch but accept per-request metadata header that runtime logs/attaches to traces. e.g.:
```proto
service RuntimeAdmission {
  rpc AddBatch(AddBatchRequest) returns (AddBatchResponse);
}
message AddBatchRequest {
  repeated Request requests = 1;
  BatchMeta meta = 2; // contains enqueue_ts, tenant_id, route
}
```

tara: would meta be mutable? e.g., runtime may want to attach kv-cache-warm bits or eviction hints. we could have a small response meta block.

alex: i like request-level ids for joins later. runtime can return per-request processing timestamps so scheduler can compute queueing vs service time. something like: response.per_request_timestamps = [{id, dequeued_ts, started_ts, finished_ts}]

kevin: that works. just watch payload size — we add overhead per request. maybe only include full per-request traces when sampling is enabled. otherwise aggregate counters.

maria: agreed — sampling + aggregation. also we need an escape hatch: if scheduler is unhealthy, runtime should accept single-request fastpath api to bypass batch admission. fallback path: `/runtime/v1/fastpath` for small low-latency ops.

sophia: operationally, how do we route fallbacks? policy lives in the control plane, scheduler will tag requests with route policy. runtime should implement a policy priority table and a simple fallback chain; config example: `priority: [fastpath, regular, degraded-model]`.

ryan: tradeoffs note: pushing batches reduces scheduler complexity but couples admission to runtime availability. pulling (scheduler asks runtime for slot) makes more RPC chatter but gives scheduler stronger placement control.

maria: tradeoff captured. proposal: hybrid — scheduler primarily pushes batches, but runtime exposes LeaseRequest/LeaseResponse for special cases (reshard, leader changes, long-tail evictions). that keeps fastpath push while preserving pull for cluster operations.

kevin: re: queueing fairness — how do we enforce tenant headroom when runtime receives a large batch from a single tenant? should runtime split it or reject?

tara: reject with `Retry-After` and a short explanation seems safest. Alternatively runtime can accept and internally split into microbatches but that complicates tracing and cost attribution.

alex: we already do kv-cache accounting per-tenant; if runtime splits, it must preserve original request ids and emit synthetic microbatch ids. more complexity. i vote reject+backpressure.

maria: looks like consensus: push batches + per-request metadata + sampling traces + fastpath endpoint + reject-on-oversize with Retry-After. i'll update the RFC appendix with a proto sketch and observability checklist.

sophia: checklist suggestions: 1) sample rate control 2) token-level counters exported to metrics 3) per-route latency histograms 4) synthetic microbatch id if splitting is implemented later 5) a `batch_size` gauge and `rejected_batches_total` counter.

ryan: also add a debug endpoint `/runtime/debug/queue` that returns current queue head counts and per-tenant headroom usage — gated behind admin auth. super useful during incidents.

kevin: +1 on debug endpoint. make sure it's rate-limited and sanitized.

deploy-bot: deploy request received for branch `feat/scheduler-boundary` — ci passed, staging rollout scheduled at 2024-11-07T17:00:00Z :rocket:

tara: fyi i'll try to prototype AddBatch + sampling traces tomorrow. if anyone has objections to the hybrid pull for special cases speak up now.

alex: no objections. one more nit: define error codes for admission: 429 (overloaded), 422 (malformed batch), 503 (runtime unhealthy). include machine-readable details.

maria: perfect. i'll push an RFC update tonight with the proto, sample telemetry dashboards, and a short playbook for `429` handling. thanks all :heart:
